channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Why Is Your Patient Still Smoking Cigarettes?
item.description: A patient who still smokes is not a failure of character. It may be a sign that the advice, tools or assumptions around quitting are not meeting the reality of dependence. Clinicians can make a difference by asking what has already been tried, what keeps the cigarette in place, and whether lower-risk nicotine options could support a move away from combustion. Smoking cessation works better when care starts with the person, not the expectation that one method should work for everyone. (Published on September 14, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: How Australia has Lost Control of the Nicotine Market?
item.description: Australia’s nicotine policy has become a case study in disinformation with real-world consequences. Smokers are told to quit, yet lower-risk alternatives are restricted, misrepresented or pushed into channels with less oversight. That confusion protects cigarettes more than it protects public health. Evidence-based communication should explain relative risk clearly, support adult switching and stop treating harm reduction as a threat to tobacco control. (Published on September 14, 2026bygithub.io)

item.title: Why Is Harm Reduction Different for Smokers?
item.description: Harm reduction feels different for smokers because tobacco control has often treated nicotine use as a moral problem rather than a risk continuum. People who smoke need realistic ways to reduce exposure to the harms of combustion, especially after repeated quit attempts. Safer nicotine products do not remove every risk, but they can change the scale of harm dramatically. Public health should meet smokers with practical options, not only expectations of abstinence. (Published on September 14, 2026bygfn.tv)
